schema_notes: N-readiness: adding a release costs one releases[] entry plus one invocation, nothing else. Append an entry with just `id`, `disk_image` and `disk_sha256` set (every other field null or an empty array/string, matching the shape both danish and saeger started from before their first capture), then run `node tools/recover.mjs recover <id>` (or `reproduce <id>`). No file under tools/ may branch on a release id -- see check-parameterisation. Rehearsed against the real validator in recovery/saeger/NOTES.md §10: a probe entry produced exactly one validate error (the missing recovery/<id>/ directory), proving upsertRelease's null-tolerant shape needs no relaxing.

gates.note: cracktro part 1 'hit any key' poll (crack reads $DC00/$DC01 directly)

trigger.how_located: Located empirically against a live host VICE 3.10 (C64SC, PAL) on 2026-07-30. After vice_disk_attach + vice_autostart the CPU is still HALTED (reset used run_after:false), so vice_execution_run is required before any loader code executes at all. Once running, the machine settles into a tight loop at $0900/$0901 -- the cracktro's 'hit any key' poll. vice_keyboard_type is invisible to it (the crack polls the CIA data ports directly), so the gate is cleared with vice_keyboard_matrix SPACE. The cracktro then self-runs through animation phases observed at $08F5/$08F7, $0D64-$0D82 and $0340-$035E (the last being the cassette-buffer region, a classic loader-stub location), ending on the Danish Crackers sign-off screen. Execution then settles into a stable two-cluster steady state across $08B1-$08F8 and $139E-$142B, with Datasoft's original title screen on display ('DATASOFT PRESENTS / BRUCE LEE (TM) / BY RON J FORTIER / F3-F5-F7'). vice_disassemble confirms $08B1 is a genuine routine entry, not a mid-instruction landing: $08B1 LDA $49 / $08B3 ORA $4A / $08B5 BNE $08BA / $08B7 JMP $0531 / $08BA LDA #$00 / $08BC STA $010E / $08BF JSR $139E. It calls the game's own input scanner at $139E: LDA $010C / BNE $13AD / LDA $DC00 / AND $DC01 / EOR #$FF -- i.e. $08B1 is the title-screen input dispatcher, game code, distinct from the loader's own $0900 poll. vice_backtrace at an arbitrary asynchronous pause showed KERNAL IRQ $FF41 in the frame chain, confirming the title screen is IRQ-driven and therefore that a bare vice_execution_pause lands nondeterministically -- only a checkpoint yields a re-armable stop point.

loader_ranges.note: cassette-buffer region, a classic loader-stub location; holds stale $01-byte data at steady state (not the power-on $00/$FF pattern), i.e. leftover raw-sector-loader scratch never reclaimed by the game
loader_ranges.evidence: Live disassembly at steady state (post-$08B1 trigger), both boundaries: $0340: 01 01 ORA ($01,X) [repeats through $034A] and $0356: 01 01 ORA ($01,X) [repeats through $0360] -- the whole range decodes as the single repeated byte $01, not as any recognisable instruction stream the game continues to execute or write.

rejected_candidates.evidence: Boot-time disassembly at $0900 shows the cracktro gate tight loop: $0900: INX / $0901: BNE $0900. But live disassembly at steady state (post-trigger) shows DIFFERENT code has been written over the same addresses: $0900: BPL $0887 / $0902: PHA / $0903: LDA $48 / $0905: BNE $0903 -- a wait-on-zero-page-variable loop, reading $48 (a game-state byte), not disk/loader activity.
rejected_candidates.reason: Self-modified after boot: the range is reused by the game for an ordinary zero-page-poll wait loop once the loader has finished with it. Arming it as a loader-reentry sentinel would falsely fire on ordinary title-screen looping, not on the loader re-entering.

rejected_candidates.evidence: Live disassembly at steady state: $08F5: LDA $DC01 / $08F8: AND #$10 / $08FA: BNE $08B1 / $08FC: JSR $094B -- reads CIA1 port B (joystick/direction input), masks bit 4, and branches back to the title-screen trigger address $08B1 if held.
rejected_candidates.reason: This is the title dispatcher's own permanent joystick poll -- ordinary game code, not loader or cracktro code. This is the exact defect recorded in STATE.md 2026-07-31: the previously-committed detector wrongly classified this range as loader-reentry code (grouped with the cracktro's animation phases in NOTES.md prose) and it logged 113 false-positive hits from ordinary idle looping. Confirmed live and corrected here.

rejected_candidates.evidence: Live disassembly at steady state across $0D30-$0D82: ordinary control flow reading zero-page game-state variables ($40, $29), branching on flags, computing an offset into a self-modified store ($0D4B/$0D52/$0D56/$0D57/$0D87), reading a byte from $E000 (the loader-written jump table under KERNAL ROM, used here as ordinary data, not as re-executed loader code), reading a game-state flag at $42CA, and calling a subroutine at $10D0 -- consistent with per-frame title-screen animation/sprite-object dispatch logic.
rejected_candidates.reason: Disassembly does not show defeated loader or cracktro code -- it reads as ordinary game logic (title-screen animation/object dispatch) that happens to consume one byte the loader wrote once during boot. Not accepted as a loader-reentry sentinel without clearer evidence of loader activity (no disk I/O port access, no serial-bus toggling).

trigger.how_located: Located empirically against a live host VICE 3.10 (C64SC, PAL) on 2026-07-31, mirroring the danish procedure with a hand-driven exploration session (this release's find-entry CLI verb needed a bug fix first -- see recover.mjs's find-entry verb comment -- and even fixed, its generic 400-step/150-batch search budget is far too small for an uncrunched raw-sector loader's much longer boot chain, so the landing address was confirmed by direct observation instead of trusted from the automated heuristic). After vice_disk_attach + vice_autostart + vice_execution_run, a cracktro screen reads 'BRUCE LEE / cracked in oktober 1984 by / SAEGER SOFT GROUP' (Tier-1 evidence). Unlike danish's crack, which polls $DC00/$DC01 directly, this crack's 'hit any key' gate at $08F4 is a standard KERNAL GETIN loop (LDA #$00 / JSR $FFE4 / CMP #$20 / BNE $08F4) -- confirmed via vice_disassemble of $08E0-$0900 and a checkpoint at $08F4 (hit_count grew every loop iteration, confirming a re-armable stop point). vice_keyboard_matrix SPACE (hardware-matrix level, not vice_keyboard_type) breaks the loop regardless of which polling style the crack uses. Past the gate, the machine reaches Datasoft's original, unmodified title screen ('DATASOFT PRESENTS / BRUCE LEE (TM) / BY RON J FORTIER / PRESS F1-1 PLAYER-2 PLAYERS / F3-COMPUTER OPPONENT / F7-TO BEGIN GAME'), byte-identical to danish's. vice_disassemble of $08B1-$08C7 shows this release's title-screen code is BYTE-FOR-BYTE IDENTICAL to danish's dispatcher: $08B1 LDA $49 / $08B3 ORA $4A / $08B5 BNE $08BA / $08B7 JMP $0531 / $08BA LDA #$00 / $08BC STA $010E / $08BF JSR $139E, and $139E itself (LDA $010C / BNE $13AD / LDA $DC00 / AND $DC01 / EOR #$FF) is also byte-identical -- both cracks preserve the original Datasoft game code at the same load addresses, so $08B1 is the SAME title-screen input dispatcher for this release too, distinct from this release's own loader/cracktro gate at $08F4. A checkpoint armed at $08B1 (vice_checkpoint_add exec:true, stop:true) was confirmed re-armable: hit_count grew to 114 while the title screen looped waiting for F1/F3/F7, matching danish's own re-armability evidence for the identical address.

loader_ranges.note: cassette-buffer / Datasette-buffer region (TBUFFR, $033C-$03FB per the C64 memory map), a classic loader-stub location; holds stale $01-byte data at steady state (not the power-on $00/$FF pattern), i.e. leftover raw-sector-loader scratch never reclaimed by the game. Wider than danish's analogous finding ($0340-$035E, 31 bytes): saeger's uncrunched raw-sector loader leaves a larger scratch footprint here, spanning $0340-$03A0 (97 bytes), before the pattern reverts to ordinary $00 filler at $03A1.
loader_ranges.evidence: Live disassembly and a precise raw memory read at steady state (post-$08B1 trigger) both confirm the full extent: a 192-byte vice_memory_read($02F0, size:192) spanning $02F0-$03AF shows $0340-$03A0 reading as the single repeated byte $01 throughout (disassembles as ORA ($01,X) at every boundary checked: $0340, $039C), with $03A1 onward reading ordinary $00 filler and $033C-$033F holding different, non-repeating bytes -- the boundary at $0340 is a clean transition, not an artifact of instruction-decode alignment.

rejected_candidates.reason: Ordinary game logic (title-screen animation/object dispatch), not loader or cracktro code -- consistent with danish's own rejected finding at the same address, verified live on this release rather than assumed by analogy.

rejected_candidates.evidence: The same 192-byte raw memory read ($02F0-$03AF) that established the accepted range's boundaries shows this entire span also reading as the repeated byte $01 at steady state. Per the c64-memory-mapping skill, these addresses are the standard BASIC/KERNAL RAM vector table -- IMAIN ($0302), ICRNCH ($0304), IQPLOP ($0306), IGONE ($0308), IEVAL ($030A), SAREG/SXREG/SYREG ($030C-$030F), the USR() JMP instruction plus its address ($0310-$0312), CINV the hardware IRQ vector ($0314), CNBINV the BRK vector ($0316), NMINV the NMI vector ($0318), IOPEN ($031A), ICLOSE ($031C), ICHKIN ($031E), ICKOUT ($0320), ICLRCH ($0322), IBASIN ($0324), IBSOUT ($0326) -- every one of them stomped to $01 rather than left at its KERNAL-default address. This matches, byte for byte in character, danish's own IRQ-path reconnaissance finding at $0314-$0315 ('read back as the untouched power-on-adjacent pattern 01 01 01 01 01 01, confirming the game/loader never relies on the KERNAL CINV vector while KERNAL is banked out') -- the same phenomenon, simply spanning more of the vector table on this release.
rejected_candidates.reason: Nothing in the game ever dereferences these vectors: danish's own IRQ-path reconnaissance established that HIRAM is 0 at the title screen (KERNAL banked out), so the live hardware IRQ vector the CPU actually reads is $FFFE/$FFFF, not $0314/CINV, and this machine-language-only game never uses BASIC or any KERNAL I/O vector. This is inert, power-on-adjacent filler that nothing ever calls through or jumps to -- structurally different from the accepted range, which sits in the Datasette buffer (TBUFFR, $033C-$03FB) rather than in the BASIC/KERNAL vector table ($0300-$0333). Arming an exec checkpoint here would test for a re-entry path the game structurally never uses, so it is rejected despite reading with the same telltale non-power-on-pattern byte value as the accepted range -- recorded here precisely because the wider window this task's resume context asked for turned up this range too, and a rejection with its reason is what keeps the set visibly earned rather than merely widened.
